3. The facts of the plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the land measuring 1.90 acres out of 10 acres appertaining to RS khatian No. 436 corresponding to SA khatian No. 517, 842, 843, 844, 845, 846, 847 and 848 of mouza. Ramkantopur under Rajbari PS originally belonged to Bishnu Mondal, Sakiron Nesa, Esem Mondal and Jobed Mondal in equal shares; that while Sakiron Nesa had been enjoying and possessing her share of 2.14 acres of land, she died leaving her only daughter Samiron Nesa alias Saju as her only heir; that Samiron Nesa died leaving one son the opposite party No. 1 and one daughter Fuljan Nesa as her heirs; that Fuljan Nesa died leaving her husband opposite party No. 2 and two sons, opposite parties Nos. 3 and 4 as her heirs; that Bishnu Mondal died leaving his wife Jarina Nesa and two sons, the opposite parties Nos. 2 and 3 and that after the death of Jarina Nesa the opposite parties Nos. 2 and 3 became her heirs. It is further stated that Jobed Mondal died leaving his wife Diljan Bibi, the proforma opposite party No. 11 and one son the plaintiff No. 1; that while the opposite parties were enjoying and possessing 2.14 acres of land out of the suit lands, the opposite party No. 1 transferred 24 decimals land of RS plot No. 813 in favour of. Md Shahjahan Mondal by sale; that while the opposite parties were enjoying and possessing 1.90 acres of land in ejmali, the petitioners and other proforma opposite parties in the first part of Kartik, 1406 BS declared that the opposite parties had no title in the suit land, that hearing this opposite parties enquired into the concerned offices and came to know that the SA record has been erroneously prepared in part; that it is seen from the SA record that 4 annas share has been recorded in the name of Sakiron Nesa; that during her life time Sakiron Nesa neither sold nor transferred any land from the suit khatian and that while the opposite parties in the first part of Chaitra 1406 BS asked the petitioners to partition their 1.90 acres of land by metes and bound, the petitioners and other proforma opposite parties denied to partition the same and hence the suit. 

 5. It is further stated that the suit land belonged to Bishnu Mondal, Sakiron Nesa, Esem Mondal and Jober Mondal in equal share; that Sakiron Nesa had another name Fuljan and her husband's name was Nasor Uddin; that while Sakiron Nesa had been enjoying and possessing her share of 2.14 acres of land in the suit khatian, she transferred 13 decimals out of 50 decimals of land of RS khatian No. 6390 by registered sale deed dated 25-10-1952 in favour of Jabber alias Jobed Ali; that Jobed Ali died leaving the petitioner No. 1 and the proforma opposite party No. 11 as his heirs and SA khatian No. 847 has been correctly prepared in their names. It is further stated that Sakiron Nesa transferred 43 decimals of land of RS plot No. 6145, 6144 and 6204 by a registered sale deed dated 5-10-1953 in favour of the proforma opposite party No. 20; that the proforma opposite party No. 20 has been enjoying and possessing the said 43 decimals of land through her husband the petitioner No. 2 and in respect of the said land, SA khatian No. 946 has been correctly prepared in her name; that in the aforesaid sale deed, the name of Sakiron Nesa has been written as Fuljan Nesa, wife of Nasor Uddin Mondal; that Sakiron also transferred 1.05 acres of land out of RS plot Nos. 6147, 6201, 6204 and 6294 by a registered sale deed dated 1-2-1958 in favour of the petitioner No. 2; that before the publication of SA record, Sakiron Nesa sold 29 decimals of land in favour of Kala Chand Sarker, the proforma opposite party No. 21 by sale and in respect of said land, SA record was prepared in his name; that in the aforesaid manner, Sakiron Nesa sold 1.90 acres of land out of 2.14 acres and while enjoying and possessing the remaining 24 decimals, she died leaving the opposite parties Nos. 1 to 4 as her heirs who sold their inherited 24 decimals of land by a registered sale deed in favour of the proforma opposite party No. 9 and became fully extinguished in the suit land; that purchaser Kala Chand and other purchasers and their successive heirs are necessary parties in the suit; that the petitioner No. 2 by filing additional written statement stated that he sold 7 decimals of land of RS plot No. 6206 in favour of the wife of opposite party No. 1 who has been enjoying and possessing the said land by erecting homestead in the western part of the plot and except the said 7 decimals, the opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 have no land in the suit land and, therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
